reason: E1 demonstrates Y2O3 dispersion strengthening in a different alloy system, supporting the general ODS mechanism, but provides no evidence for TiVNbTa specifically, nor for stability or strengthening at 1273 K. E2 discusses solid-solution strengthening in other refractory alloys and is irrelevant to Y2O3 dispersoids. Thus, the key premises regarding uniform incorporation, high-temperature stability, and quantitative strengthening in TiVNbTa are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Nano-scale Y2O3 dispersoids can be uniformly incorporated into a refractory high-entropy alloy matrix via powder metallurgy and spark plasma sintering.
Y2O3 dispersoids will remain stable and coherent in the TiVNbTa matrix at 1273 K without forming deleterious phases.
Oxide dispersion strengthening (ODS) via Y2O3 effectively obstructs dislocation motion and inhibits grain growth at elevated temperatures in refractory alloys.
The ODS mechanism will yield a 20–50% increase in yield strength at 1273 K over the baseline TiVNbTa alloy.
